summary: Generates, converts, and exposes timecode as CHOP channels and a Python Timecode object from timeline, string, parameter, channel, or OP timecode sources.
key_concepts: Timecode CHOP generates timecode as both CHOP channels and a Python `.timecode` member.
Mode selects the source: timeline, index, timecode string, parameters, sequential playback, Timecode object, CHOP channels, or an OP timecode member.
SMPTE mode enforces non-negative timecode, rates up to 60 fps, and a 24-hour loop; general mode allows negative timecode and a longer 100-hour range.
Input CHOP channels named `negative`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, or `frame` are added to the generated timecode.
Drop-frame handling compensates when a fractional FPS is rounded to whole frames, with automatic handling for common standards such as 29.97.
Output toggles choose component channels such as negative, hour, minute, second, frame, total seconds, total frames, drop-frame, and FPS.

key_params.name: smpte
key_params.note: Use SMPTE limits: non-negative, <=60 fps, 24-hour loop

key_params.name: extendright

common_gotchas: Timecode CHOP outputs both CHOP channel data and a .timecode Python member.
SMPTE mode disallows negative timecode and loops at 24 hours; general mode allows negative values and up to 100 hours.
When driven by channels, named input channels such as negative, hour, minute, second, and frame are added to output.
Timecode string mode expects standard timecode-style formatting.
Use Timeline CHOP when the goal is component timeline channels rather than general timecode conversion.
Drop-frame and FPS choices need to match media/device expectations.
